raw_response:
I would start with **Qwen Code paired with an open-weight Qwen3-Coder model**. Your wording could mean the terminal agent, the model behind it, or the combination, so the useful choices are configurations rather than just application names. Qwen's dated announcement describes Qwen Code as a command-line agent adapted for Qwen3-Coder; its current repository also documents local Ollama and vLLM support. [Qwen Code](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code) · [Qwen announcement](https://qwenlm.github.io/blog/qwen3-coder/)

1. **Qwen Code + Qwen3-Coder** is my first choice for a closely matched terminal-agent/model pairing. A concrete downloadable model is [Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct), whose official card lists Apache-2.0 and model-loading instructions. Choose that kind of public checkpoint explicitly; the fact that an agent offers a Qwen-branded hosted service is not by itself proof that the selected service model has public weights.

2. **[OpenCode](https://opencode.ai/) + an open-weight model through Ollama** is an attractive option if you want to choose the model separately from the terminal interface. Its [provider documentation](https://opencode.ai/docs/providers/) describes local Ollama models and custom OpenAI-compatible endpoints. Check the configured model's tool-call support: the current documentation says vLLM discovery initially disables tools because it cannot infer their support. I am recommending the documented configuration route, not claiming I tested that combination or that every model works equally well.

3. **[goose](https://goose-docs.ai/) + an open-weight model** is particularly relevant to your use of the terminal for things beyond coding. Its official description includes research, writing, automation, and data analysis. The [Ollama project's integration guide](https://github.com/ollama/ollama/blob/main/docs/integrations/goose.mdx) documents configuring the goose CLI with Ollama and selecting a model. The useful behavior still depends on that model and the tools you enable.

4. **[Aider](https://aider.chat/) + a local open-weight model** is worth considering if repository editing and pair programming account for most of the work. It documents an [Ollama connection](https://aider.chat/docs/llms/ollama.html) using `aider --model ollama_chat/<model>`. I would treat it as a narrower coding option; the reviewed documentation does not establish a replacement for every unspecified non-coding task.

5. **[Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct)** is also a model-only answer to the ambiguous request. It supplies weights, but you still need an inference runtime and terminal agent to obtain the workflow. Qwen Code is the most directly documented pairing in this shortlist.

These are documentation-based options, not a claim of Claude-level quality or feature parity. Your hardware, platform, and task mix were not supplied, so I cannot determine which checkpoint fits locally. The Qwen family/CLI announcement predates the 2026-11-01 question, while most pages reviewed are undated live documentation; their exact feature state on that date remains unverified.
